accounts.name: Columbia (NYP)
accounts.situation: Fastest-growing account by revenue. McKhann runs mostly primary-tumor LITT (12 primary, 2 mets) over an enormous epilepsy, neuro-onc and referral base. McKhann is leaving for Emory; Gill is the successor. Brett Youngerman shows 2 LITT in claims not in our log (Visualase?), with an in-house Visualase rep on site.

accounts.name: Yale New Haven
accounts.situation: Territory flagship and strongest relationship. Chiang is a disclosed Monteris consultant and the dominant necrosis author (48 mets/RN, only 2 primary, no recurrent). Epilepsy LITT program is weak through Damisah, who has high affinity for open crani. Volume limited by internal politics.

accounts.name: Brigham & Women's
accounts.situation: Revenue fell from $361K to $15K under a ClearPoint capital threat from the Mass General Brigham merger — Mark Richardson (MGH) is a paid ClearPoint consultant pushing system standardization. Golby is the senior tumor champion who actively defended us. Rolston knows our system but wants to align with Richardson.

accounts.name: Beth Israel Deaconess
accounts.situation: Stalled tumor-only account. Vega (primary user) disengaged over MRI friction; claims show 16 LITT against the 4 logged. Josh Aronson may be using Visualase. Outside-indication research teed up (cavernous malformations with Ogilvy's endovascular team).

accounts.name: Nemours Children's (DE)
accounts.situation: New NeuroBlate account, just closed, extending south into Delaware pediatrics. Catherine Wassef (Colorado-trained pediatric neurosurgeon, epilepsy + MIS focus) is the champion. Lily Tran leaving for Yale.

accounts.name: University of Vermont
accounts.situation: Active opportunity, northern New England anchor. Penar is senior neurosurgeon, Liebelt newer faculty; no LITT there yet. Landing capital and confirming a committed first user.

accounts.name: Mount Sinai
accounts.situation: Two real laser surgeons: Fedor Panov (8 LITT, 104 intractable-epilepsy patients) and Saadi Ghatan (4, chair-level). Largest untapped epilepsy pool in the plan, opened through Panov and LAANTERN. Monteris revenue on the books with zero logged cases — verify what is running.

accounts.name: Westchester Medical Center
accounts.situation: Growing across Muh, Hanft and Sukul. Hanft came out of the Danish Visualase school and now runs NeuroBlate — a live conversion reference for nearby Visualase-trained surgeons. Steven Wolf drives epilepsy referrals.

accounts.name: Boston Children's
accounts.situation: Highest LITT volume anywhere in the territory (85 cases / 3 yr, ~28/yr, ~$518K none of it ours). Scellig Stone runs the program (66 cases). Platform unknown — effort here is blind until confirmed. NeuroBlate reportedly once installed; switched over Monteris personnel changes, not technology.

accounts.name: NYU Langone
accounts.situation: Growing across a four-surgeon base (Rozman, Dastagirzada, Placantonakis, Hidalgo). Diffuse momentum that must concentrate in one or two drivers.

accounts.name: Stony Brook
accounts.situation: Mikell drives essentially all volume (epilepsy + some tumor). Single-surgeon concentration is the risk — one departure from zero. Needs a second adopter.

accounts.name: Hackensack Meridian — JFK (Edison, NJ)
accounts.situation: Two of our users here (Milano, Shekhtman) at JFK in Edison NJ. Hackensack Meridian is a large multi-hospital system — JFK is one entry point into a much bigger footprint (Jersey Shore, Hackensack UMC). Hackensack UMC is a SEPARATE competitive target (Danish, Visualase, 33 LITT).

accounts.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering
accounts.situation: Near-zero open neurosurgery, so this is a referral play, not surgeon conversion. Decline is upstream in neuro-onc and rad-onc. Souweidane (top pediatric neurosurgeon) WANTS TO START A PROGRAM AT CORNELL.

accounts.name: Jersey Shore (Hackensack Meridian)
accounts.situation: Shabbar Danish is the highest-volume laser surgeon in the Hackensack Meridian network (9 LITT here + 31 at Hackensack UMC). A Monteris system is already in value analysis at Jersey Shore awaiting a trial — an active deal, not a cold account.

accounts.name: Temple University Hospital
accounts.situation: Quiet account. Scott Shepard drives volume, trending up, revenue capture 1.27x territory average (complex, valuable cases). Metastasis-weighted with little epilepsy work. Single-surgeon dependent; claims undercount (1 LITT claims vs 10 logged).

accounts.name: Rochester General
accounts.situation: Kimmell is our user, primarily tumor. Workflow is the constraint (bolt in OR, transport to GE scanner, close in recovery). Probe restock 0.75 (lowest), revenue capture 0.62x (lowest). Site-identity data issues.

accounts.name: Upstate University Hospital
accounts.situation: Lost Zulma Tovar-Spinoza (left for South Carolina); volume fell with her. Knudsen is new (first epilepsy case in March) — effectively restarting. No tumor work. Sits on ~1,073 intractable-epilepsy patients, one of the largest DRE pools in the territory. Miller carries 19 epilepsy cranis.

accounts.name: Weill Cornell
accounts.situation: Quiet account with two logged cases; claims show zero LITT against our two. Real opening is external: Mark Souweidane (MSK) wants to start a program at Cornell, which would convert a dormant account into a surgeon-led build.

evidence.title: Interstitial Thermal Therapy in Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
evidence.cite: Landazuri P et al. JAMA Neurology 2025;82(9):915-924
evidence.finding: Largest prospective MTLE LITT cohort (145 pts, 15 sites). 2-yr Engel I ~58.4% / ILAE 1-2 57.2%; durable. vs a historical control, Engel I at 12 mo 60.6% (LITT) vs 8% (medical management), OR 18.5 (95% CI 5.6-59.5). Severe AE ~2.1%; >1/3 reduced/stopped ASMs.
evidence.supports: The flagship modern MTLE paper — durable seizure freedom comparable to open surgery and dramatically better than continued medication. The single strongest counter to under-referral.

evidence.title: Effects of Surgical Targeting in LITT for MTLE (234 patients)
evidence.finding: 1-yr 58.0% Engel I / 77.1% Engel I-II; stable at 2 yr. Targeting/anatomy drives outcomes.
evidence.supports: Credibility with functional neurosurgeons — durable outcomes achievable with careful targeting.

evidence.title: Prospective Multicenter Study of Laser Ablation for DRE — 1-Year Outcomes
evidence.cite: Landazuri P et al. Epilepsy Research 2020;167:106473
evidence.finding: 64.3% Engel I, 73.8% Engel I-II at 1 yr; 72% QoL improvement; median LOS 32.7h; 84% prefer minimally invasive.
evidence.supports: The broad epilepsy story: meaningful seizure freedom + QoL + short stay. The enemy is under-referral.

evidence.title: ASSFN Position Statement on LITT for Drug-Resistant Epilepsy
evidence.finding: 25-40% of epilepsy is drug-resistant; only ~4% of eligible DRE patients get surgery. LITT seizure freedom 44-78% at 1 yr.
evidence.supports: Society backing for LITT in DRE and the under-treatment gap that defines the epilepsy opportunity.

evidence.title: LITT + adjuvant pembrolizumab in recurrent high-grade astrocytoma
evidence.cite: Campian JL et al. Nature Communications 2026;17(1):1763
evidence.finding: >3x improved overall survival with NeuroBlate + pembrolizumab; LITT triggers an enhanced immune response and a more favorable tumor micro-environment; safe & well-tolerated.
evidence.supports: The strongest GBM evidence yet — a Phase 1/randomized Phase 2b showing LITT-immunotherapy synergy. Opens a new care-pathway conversation for recurrent HGG.

evidence.title: Efficacy of LITT for Newly Diagnosed and Recurrent IDH-Wildtype GBM
evidence.cite: de Groot JF et al. Neuro-Oncol Adv 2022;4(1):vdac040
evidence.finding: nGBM median OS ~16.1 mo, PFS ~11.9 mo; rGBM median OS ~9 mo — comparable to published resection ranges in selected patients.
evidence.supports: The core GBM paper: an option when open resection is unsafe, deep, or undesirable. Cytoreductive, not curative.

evidence.title: LITT + SRT increases time to progression for recurrent brain metastases
evidence.cite: Grabowski M et al. Neuro-Oncol Adv 2022;4(1):vdac086
evidence.finding: Median freedom from local progression 29.8 mo (LITT+SRT) vs 7.5 (LITT alone) vs 3.7 (SRT alone); median OS 12.7 vs 5.9 vs 6.2 mo (n=55).
evidence.supports: LITT+SRT is superior to either modality alone for biopsy-proven recurrent mets after SRT failure — a combination-therapy story for rad-onc.

evidence.title: 12-Month Outcomes and QoL After Brain Tumor Ablation (LAANTERN)
evidence.finding: Median stay ~33.4h; >83% discharged home; 12-mo OS ~73%; low 30-day readmission.
evidence.supports: The patient-centered oncology recovery story: short stay, home discharge, preserved QoL in a real-world tumor cohort.

evidence.title: LITT and Early Intervention for Progression Following SRS
evidence.finding: LITT vs steroids alone for biopsy-proven RN in previously radiated mets — reduces steroid dependence and steroid-induced morbidity; complication ~5% (vs up to 7% for biopsy alone).
evidence.supports: Post-SRS progression = recurrence vs RN uncertainty. LITT combines biopsy + treatment + steroid reduction in one procedure.

evidence.title: LITT for Biopsy-Proven Radiation Necrosis in Recurrent Brain Mets
evidence.cite: Chan M et al. Neuro-Oncol Adv 2023;5(1):vdad031
evidence.finding: Median hospitalization ~32.5h; median steroid cessation 13 days; ~19% lesional progression at 1 yr (n=90, 14 sites).
evidence.supports: One of the cleanest value props — gets patients off steroids so systemic/immunotherapy can continue.

evidence.title: LITT for New and Recurrent Meningioma: A Prospective and Retrospective Case Series
evidence.cite: Chiang VL et al. J Neurosurg 2024 Mar 8:1-11
evidence.finding: Largest LITT meningioma cohort to date (n=20); 1-yr local control 61.4% for patients with >=91% ablation; safe, well-tolerated; no radiation-necrosis contribution and no dose ceiling.
evidence.supports: Opens a NEW indication — a minimally invasive option for aggressive/recurrent meningioma (WHO grade 2-3) that has exhausted resection and radiation. Lead author Chiang is at Yale.

evidence.title: AANS/CNS Position Statement on MR-guided LITT for Brain Tumors & RN
evidence.finding: Up to 49% of tumors are in/near eloquent areas; NCCN (2024) includes LITT for poor surgical candidates, recurrent mets, RN, glioblastoma and other gliomas.
evidence.supports: Society + guideline backing across the tumor pathway — deep-seated, eloquent, recurrent, and poor-surgical-candidate lesions.

evidence.title: LAANTERN Procedural Safety and Hospitalization
evidence.finding: Short hospitalization, little/no ICU, most discharged home; LITT-related complication ~5%.
evidence.supports: The safety/operations answer: LITT behaves more like a stereotactic procedure than an open craniotomy.
